text:
laura: Heads-up — seeing a sustained 95th pct latency bump on the continuous-batcher pool (prod, us-west) starting ~09:15 UTC after the prefetch-fence heuristic landed. Investigating.

sam: saw it on the dashboard too. qps stable, p95 up ~120ms -> +40ms vs yesterday. throughput flat, but CPU on GPU nodes slightly higher.

devin: can you paste the job id? I’ll grep logs and run a profile.

laura: job=rbw-batcher-v2.2.3, rollout cassandra at 09:12. quick trace: `kernel_choice=fast_attn_v2 -> fallback=generic_attn` on a subset of microbatches when prefetch fence engaged.

marta: that kernel flip smells like shape-triggered routing. The fence might be changing arrival shapes and token budgets -> wrong kernel affinity.

ryan: I pulled a perf trace from one affected trace:
```
batch_id=0x7f3c tokens=[8,96,12,4] prefetch_fence=ENABLED
selected_kernel=fast_attn_v2
at_token=34: kernel_switch -> generic_attn (cost delta +28ms)
kv_hits=partial, kv_lock_time=12ms
queue_wait=5ms
```

sam: interesting - kv_lock_time spikes when the fence glues prefetch and kv priming. That + kernel switch explains the tail.

devin: running a small experiment locally: disable fence for models with avg seq < 32 and see if kernel affinity stabilizes. Also want to check token_budget math — fence might be inflating the projected batch token count causing premature small-batch routing.

laura: can you run this quick query to get token_budget skew? `select token_budget, batch_size, shapes from traces where prefetch_fence=1 and ts>1765432000 limit 200`

ops-bot: query job launched (job id q-98123). ETA ~90s.

marta: FYI I also saw an uptick in KV eviction churn in the same window — eviction rate +3x. Could be GC interplay when fence pins prefetch buffers.

ryan: I dumped one worker's scheduler log (trimmed):
```
[09:16:02] enq req id=... shape=(12) est_tokens=48 -> put_in_microqueue T=9ms
[09:16:02] prefetch-fence wait for kv-priming T=11ms
[09:16:02] microbatch formed size=4 tokens_total=160 -> choose_kernel=fast_attn_v2
[09:16:02] at token=32 kernel_switch->generic_attn (fallback path)
```

sam: two leads: 1) the fence introduces a kv priming wait that changes per-batch shape distribution; 2) token_budget calc uses prefetch window size and may be overconstraining merge decisions.

devin: I ran the local A/B toggles: Turning off fence drops p95 by ~35ms on a synthetic replay of the same QPS/shapes (10k reqs). Throughput identical.

laura: good. Is there a safe runtime flag to limit fence to large batches only? We could roll a hotfix that gates fence for avg_batch_tokens < 128.

marta: we have runtime flag `prefetch.fence.min_batch_tokens`. default=32. It looks like the rollout changed default to 16 in the canary config by accident. That would explain why small batches are getting fenced.

ryan: omg that explains a ton. If fence=16 we prime for very small shapes -> higher kv contention and more kernel switches.

sam: propose hotpatch: revert default to 64 (safer), and add a temporary kernel affinity override that pins to generic_attn for mixed shapes until we flush telemetry.

devin: I’ll prepare the patch: 1) config rollback to 64, 2) add telemetry spike tag `prefetch_fence_rollback` so we can filter. Planning to roll to canary and then prod.

laura: timeline?

devin: patch ready in 12m, canary roll 15m after that, monitor for 30m.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline started (deploy id d-4421)

marta: re-check KV metrics after canary — eviction and lock time should drop. If not, we may need to tweak token_budget formula (look at `prefetch_window * shape_variance`).

sam: after rollback to 64, my quick replay shows p95 back to baseline and kernel_switch events reduced by ~90%. KV_lock_time median down to 3ms.

laura: awesome. After canary completes let's prepare a postmortem note: root cause = inadvertent default change for prefetch.fence.min_batch_tokens -> increased fencing of small batches -> KV priming contention -> kernel selection flip -> p95 tail. Mitigation = default rollback + telemetry + stricter rollout gating.

ryan: also add a unit test for token_budget calc with fence toggles so future defaults can't accidentally regress this.

devin: will open PR with changes + test. tagging @oncall for visibility.

laura: thanks team. monitoring looks clean so far. follow-up doc in #eng-runtime with perf graphs and exact rollout diff. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy d-4421 canary succeeded, promoted to prod at 09:53 UTC.
